parameter_rationale.model: deepseek-v4-pro is selected over deepseek-v4-flash for final taxonomy construction because this is a manuscript-support semantic coding task where accuracy and careful definition-following are more important than cost/latency. Deprecated aliases such as deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner are avoided.
parameter_rationale.thinking_disabled: DeepSeek documentation states thinking mode does not support temperature/top_p controls. Thinking is disabled so deterministic low-temperature classification parameters are active and reportable.
parameter_rationale.temperature: 0 is used for deterministic/focused classification with a fixed label set. The task is closer to controlled coding than open-ended data analysis.
parameter_rationale.top_p: 1 is kept at the neutral/default nucleus setting; temperature is the active sampling control.
parameter_rationale.json_object: JSON output mode is used so the API guarantees syntactically valid JSON; the prompt also explicitly instructs JSON-only output.

source_scope.unit_of_llm_classification: unique Retraction Watch raw Reason item, not individual retraction record
source_scope.main_analysis_records: RetractionNature == Retraction; main annual figures use 2000-2025 and exclude 2026 partial year

research_content_reliability.label: Research-content reliability
research_content_reliability.definition: Signals that the reliability, reproducibility, validity, or evidentiary integrity of the research content itself is questioned.
include: computer/AI-generated article content when it affects content authenticity
paper-mill or fabricated article production when it indicates article-level reliability risk
exclude: journal/publisher procedural acts without a content reliability signal
research_content_reliability.manuscript_link: Supports discussion of the reliability of the published product/scientific record, without assigning fault.

attribution_authorship_disclosure_integr.label: Attribution, authorship, and disclosure integrity
attribution_authorship_disclosure_integr.definition: Signals concerning who created, approved, owned, disclosed, cited, or was credited for the work, including attribution and disclosure problems.
exclude: generic data/image/results unreliability without attribution/authorship/disclosure element
attribution_authorship_disclosure_integr.manuscript_link: Matches the manuscript's concern with transparent relationships among authors, editors, reviewers, and publishers and with disclosure/attribution integrity.

editorial_peer_review_governance.label: Editorial and peer-review governance
editorial_peer_review_governance.definition: Signals that editorial decision-making, peer review, journal/publisher procedures, or editorial independence/governance mechanisms are implicated.
include: publication-policy breach or sanction when it concerns publication governance
exclude: journal/publisher investigation as source only unless the reason itself concerns editorial/peer-review procedure
content unreliability without editorial or peer-review process signal
editorial_peer_review_governance.manuscript_link: Directly supports the manuscript's themes of peer-review integrity, editorial independence, proportionality, and governance.

post_publication_transparency_due_proces.label: Post-publication transparency, due process, and oversight
post_publication_transparency_due_proces.definition: Signals concerning post-publication investigation, notice transparency, correction/retraction status, availability/removal, procedural communication, institutional/legal oversight, or appeal/objection-related process.
include: notice lacks information or is inaccessible
exclude: data/image/results problems without post-publication process information
peer-review compromise as pre-publication process unless linked to post-publication oversight
attribution/authorship issues without procedural transparency/oversight component
post_publication_transparency_due_proces.manuscript_link: Matches the manuscript's core language on transparency, clear reasons, proportionality, due process, appeal, and publisher/journal oversight.

system_prompt: You are a meticulous research-integrity taxonomy coder for a Nature-targeted manuscript. Classify Retraction Watch reason terms using only the reason name and the official definition supplied by the user. Do not use keyword matching. Do not assign legal, moral, causal, or fault responsibility. Retraction Watch reasons are curated, non-exclusive metadata signals. Investigation-by-X means the source or location of investigation, not fault by X. Notice/status terms describe metadata transparency or publication-status information, not necessarily the original cause. Return valid JSON only.
user_prompt_template:
Classify this single Retraction Watch reason item. Use the four manuscript-facing categories exactly as defined in the supplied configuration. Categories are non-exclusive; assign all that are semantically supported by the official definition. If no main category is justified, return an empty manuscript_categories array and explain why in caution.

Allowed manuscript category ids: research_content_reliability, attribution_authorship_disclosure_integrity, editorial_peer_review_governance, post_publication_transparency_due_process_oversight.

Also return low-level semantic fields for auditability. Allowed problem_object labels: data, image, results_conclusions, methods_materials, text_article, references_attribution, authorship_affiliation, ethics_welfare, legal_rights, article_general, availability_notice_status. Allowed process_signal labels: peer_review_compromised, peer_review_concern, journal_publisher_investigation, third_party_investigation, institutional_investigation, official_misconduct_process, journal_publisher_error, notice_opacity, removal_availability, editorial_breach, paper_mill, ai_computer_content, publication_policy_or_sanction, correction_update_process, legal_process, authorship_publication_process, research_ethics_approval_process, content_reuse_or_duplication_process. Allowed actor_context labels: author, editor, journal_publisher, company_institution, third_party, ori_government, unclear. actor_context means mentioned/source/procedure context, not blame.

Return one JSON object with exactly these keys: raw_reason, canonical_reason, definition_used, problem_object, process_signal, actor_context, manuscript_categories, classification_strength, main_figure_recommended, caution, semantic_rationale. classification_strength must be one of strict, broad, ambiguous. main_figure_recommended is true only if at least one manuscript category is sufficiently supported for main-figure prevalence; false for status-only, extremely ambiguous, or non-substantive labels. semantic_rationale must be concise and grounded in the definition.
